• What are the differences between a conlang and a language that typically is not called a conlang?

  • Could a conlang be simply written/spoken or would it need to contain both?

  • Could the language(s) widely accepted to be the first one(s) be called conlangs?
A few questions from a noob, not all of which are noobish.

A language that isn't a constructed one would be a natural language, one that developed organically and changes over time as people use it to communicate with the people (and animals, if you're me) around them. Conlangs can serve the same function, but they were purposely constructed rather than developing organically.

A conlang doesn't need to be both written and spoken, or either. You could make a con-sign language.

I have no idea. We'd have to find out how the first languages were made. If they were constructed purposely, then maybe, yes. But that's a bit beyond me.

Disclaimer: it's 2am here so there might be mistakes, and it may or may not make sense.

• A conlang is a language that has been constructed. Constructed language. There are other types of constructs that may seem like a conlang, but actually aren't. Some of these take the grammar from a natural language (called a natlang) and simply change the words. Essentially redressing tye language they started with. This is called a relex.

  • A conlang doesn't need to be spoken to be considered a language. It can be an only written language, or it could go so far as to only be displayed in binary, if you'd like. So long as it can be used in some way to communicate, it could be a conlang.

  • I'd say no, no it couldn't. Mostly because it would have developed naturally, and not by design. If someone had sat down and created it, then taught it to humans, then it would have been a conlang, but it most likely was created naturally by the first humans (or whatever) who spoke it.
